extracted.intended_audience: educated readers and students of philosophy/natural science interested in a unified theory of evolution
extracted.subtask_description: A synthetic, philosophical account that formulates evolution as a universal process applying to cosmical, geological, biological, psychological, and social phenomena — characterizing evolution in terms of redistribution of matter and motion and seeking to deduce these phenomena from the Persistence of Force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evolution formula: integration of matter and concomitant dissipation of motion
rubrics_metrics.description: "Evolution is an integration of matter and concomitant dissipation of motion; during which the matter passes from an indefinite, incoherent homogeneity to a definite, coherent heterogeneity; and during which the retained motion undergoes a parallel transformation."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as the concise, final formula summarizing the conception of Evolution. The surrounding text explains that with each redistribution of matter there necessarily goes a redistribution of motion, and that both structural (matter) and functional (motion) changes must be contemplated together.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universal traits of Evolution: integration, heterogeneity, definiteness
rubrics_metrics.description: Evolution is characterized by advance toward a more integrated, heterogeneous, and definite distribution of component matter and of retained motion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrated across domains: nebular condensation and planetary motions becoming integrated and definite; atmospheric and oceanic circulations becoming definite trade-winds and currents as Earth cools; crustal motions becoming larger-scale and regionally distinct; organisms' motions becoming integrated and specialized; societies' functions differentiating and coordinating. Used as a diagnostic set of traits for identifying evolutionary progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redistribution of retained motion parallels redistribution of component matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever matter in an aggregate is re-distributed during evolution, the retained motion of that aggregate is also re-distributed in parallel, producing changes in the aggregate's motions and rhythms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include: differing angular velocities in a nebulous ring becoming uniform as a mass condenses; atmospheric currents emerging as Earth's temperature gradients develop; the integration of alimentary, circulatory and respiratory functions in organisms; social functions (e.g., military, trade) becoming more multiform and coordinated as societies grow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partitioning of incident force: effective vs non-effective; temporary vs permanent; insensible vs sensible
rubrics_metrics.description: Any incident force divides into effective and non-effective portions; the effective portion further divides into temporarily effective (vibrational, radiating undulations) and permanently effective (bringing lasting re-arrangements). Permanently effective changes are of two kinds: insensible (molecular/chemical rearrangements) and sensible (mass transpositions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text explains mechanical and thermal examples (impacts, light/heat, molecular changes) to distinguish these categories. The distinction is fundamental for explaining how forces produce qualitative (molecular) and structural (sensible displacement) changes during evolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complementarity and inverse variation among force partitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The subdivisions of an incident force are complementary: the temporarily effective and permanently effective portions vary inversely; likewise, within the permanently effective portion, generation of insensible (molecular) rearrangements and sensible (structural) rearrangements are inversely related in amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stated as a general principle: where much force is expended temporarily (e.g., vibrations), less remains to produce permanent rearrangement; and among permanent effects, emphasis on molecular vs mass re-arrangement trades off. This relation is used to reason about how different kinds of changes accompany evolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instability of the homogeneous (homogeneity is unstable equilibrium)
rubrics_metrics.description: A state of perfect homogeneity is a condition of unstable equilibrium: any minute disturbance will destroy the homogeneous arrangement and produce heterogeneity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: perfectly balanced scales will eventually tip; uniformly distributed mutually-attractive particles will cluster; a perfectly uniform fluid will develop currents under unequal radiation; a uniformly heated mass will cool unequally; surface oxidation of metals produces outer parts unlike inner parts. This principle is used to argue that rearrangement (and hence evolution) must occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional differentiation and subsequent integration (coordination) in organisms and societies
rubrics_metrics.description: As structure becomes more complex, functions subdivide into distinct subordinate functions (differentiation), and these subdivided functions become coordinated into integrated systems serving common ends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Biological examples: alimentary function subdividing into secretory/absorbent regions and becoming integrated with circulatory and nervous functions; locomotion evolving from ciliary homogeneous movements to integrated limb movements. Social examples: military function differentiating into infantry, cavalry, artillery and into ranks/commissariat, then being integrated under command; governmental and commercial processes becoming more multiform and coordinated as societies scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Psychical/mental development parallels physical integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes in consciousness (subjective phenomena) correspond to nervous excitations (objective processes) and follow the same evolutionary pattern: increasing variety, definiteness, and integration of mental functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrations include infant speech progressing from homogeneous inarticulate noises to articulated, heterogeneous, and integrated language; cognitive development from simple recognition/classification to reasoning, induction/deduction, and specialized mental modes (mathematics, music, poetry); feelings becoming coordinated in adults versus impulsive in children. The mental changes are presented as correlative to nervo-muscular changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim to deduce Evolution from the Persistence of Force
rubrics_metrics.description: The phenomena and universal traits of Evolution should be interpretable (deducible) from the fundamental principle of the Persistence of Force; evolution is to be unified with simpler mechanical laws by reference to that ultimate principle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author proposes that already-seen laws (equivalence of transformed forces, motion following the line of least resistance, universal rhythmicity) are deducible from Persistence of Force; similarly the redistribution laws (integration, heterogeneity, definiteness, rhythms) ought to be shown as necessary consequences of the same ultimate principle, thereby producing a synthetic, unified explanation.
